body_long:
Monte-Carlo Société des Bains de Mer closed the sixth Festival des Etoilés Monte-Carlo on Saturday 14 November 2026 with a grand dinner in the Salle Empire of the Hôtel de Paris Monte-Carlo. The group shared the details in a press release on 16 November.

## Four chefs at one table

The closing gala brought together Alain Ducasse and Emmanuel Pilon of Le Louis XV–Alain Ducasse, Marcel Ravin of Blue Bay and Yannick Alléno of Pavyllon Monte-Carlo. Pastry chef Cedric Grolet joined them for dessert. Around 120 guests sat at two royal tables, among them Louis and Marie Ducruet and the actress Sonia Rolland.

## Versailles on the Rock

The evening was built as a Versailles-inspired dinner in four movements, with a light romantic play performed between courses. The Italian artist Valeria Romeo designed the invitation and programme, with a nod to toile de Jouy. Grolet's dessert was a trompe-l'œil soufflé named after Madame de Pompadour.

## A cellar to match

Head Sommelier Maxime Pastor led the pairings with the Hôtel de Paris cellar team. The list ran from Perrier-Jouët Belle Epoque 2018 to Château Margaux 2014 and Château d'Yquem 2016.

## Six months of four-hands dinners

The festival ran from 13 May to 14 November. Each dinner paired a resort chef with a guest: Glenn Viel at Blue Bay, Christophe Moret at Le Grill, Gérald Passedat at Pavyllon, Christopher Coutanceau at Elsa, Martino Ruggieri at L'Abysse, and Björn Frantzén at Le Louis XV. Chairman and CEO Stéphane Valeri thanked Alain Ducasse for opening the way and dedicated the festival to the chefs and teams. A seventh edition is planned for 2027.

The festival closes a strong autumn for the group's kitchens. On 4 November, Le Louis XV–Alain Ducasse entered The World's 50 Best Restaurants at number 47, a first for Monaco.

## The signal

SBM says it holds ten Michelin stars in Monaco. The festival shows how a resort can treat that collection as a single programme rather than a list of restaurants. A season-long calendar of four-hands dinners gives local regulars and international guests a reason to return, and lets the Hôtel de Paris own the closing night. For hotel groups with several starred tables, the lesson is clear: chefs are a destination in themselves when they are staged together.

summary: On 14 November, Alain Ducasse, Emmanuel Pilon, Marcel Ravin and Yannick Alléno, with Cedric Grolet on dessert, closed the sixth Festival des Etoilés Monte-Carlo with a Versailles-inspired dinner for 120 guests at the Hôtel de Paris.
title: Ducasse, Alléno and Ravin close the Festival des Etoilés Monte-Carlo
why: Monaco's biggest names in one room: SBM turns its ten Michelin stars into a season-long programme.
